Neuromancer, first edition

William Gibson’s 1984 novel, published by Ace Books with a cover by James Warhola, which set the terms of cyberpunk: cyberspace, the matrix, and jacking in.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: Neuromancer was published by Ace Books on 1 July 1984, with a first-edition cover by James Warhola. Wikipedia.

It “remains the first and only novel to win all three of the Hugo Award, the Nebula Award for Best Novel, and the Philip K. Dick Award”. Wikipedia.

Wikipedia’s Cyberpunk article notes that the novel is set in Chiba, Japan, and that its influence “dominated the early cyberpunk movement”. Cyberpunk.

Why it belongs

The book gives the style its ideas rather than its pictures: a city of data, terminals, and bodies wired into machines. Designers turn these into terminal type, data panels, and HUD frames.

Its Japanese setting links it to the same Tokyo and Hong Kong imagery as Blade Runner and Akira.

Borrow

Name panels and controls with short technical terms and codes, as the novel names its systems.
